spec_match.rationale: Recreates the explainer's Example 2 exactly: a horizontally scrollable strip with taller-than-viewport cards, comparing overflow: scroll hidden (hidden = scrollable value, script can move it) against overflow: scroll clip (clip axis pinned at 0), driven by real scrollIntoView and scrollTop assignments.

interactive.rationale: Per-strip scrollIntoView(card 8), scrollTop += 40, and Reset buttons all mutate the real containers; live per-strip readouts update on every scroll event including user drags.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The blurb promises two identical carousels where scrollIntoView and script scrolling show the pinning difference; that is precisely what the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: Shows the unrecoverable-state failure (hidden axis moved, user cannot scroll it back), the offset card that forces block-axis adjustment, and the readouts explain the observed value in both supported and coerced browsers.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5067363861004288, the spec section, and the explainer's Example 2 specifically.

conformance.rationale: clip-axis-rejects-programmatic-scroll and hidden-remains-programmatically-scrollable in the feature suite encode exactly the two behaviors this page contrasts; both executed on Chromium 141 with the honest fail/pass split.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141: after scrollIntoView both strips honestly showed scrollTop 52 with the rose readout ('clip was coerced to hidden in this browser'), card top labels visibly chopped in the screenshot, console clean. The pinned-at-0 branch needs a 152+ browser to observe.

telemetry_health.rationale: sasc-carousel-clip-axis-pinned only fires on a supporting browser; coerced browsers report sasc-carousel-legacy-fallback with the observed computed value instead.

design_system.rationale: Card labels are accent-blue on paper (AA), readout emphasis uses accent-rose/emerald on stone, all colours via variables, buttons keep the global styling.

accessibility.rationale: Strips are keyboard-focusable labelled group regions, all actions are native buttons, per-strip readouts are role=status aria-live=polite text equivalents of the visual state, and the failure state is described in words, not just visually.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×1600 with autorun: no horizontal page overflow (the strips scroll internally), buttons wrap without clipping, readouts legible; console clean apart from the environmental fonts.googleapis failure.

openQuestions.title: Verify the pinned branch and consider a scroll-snap variant on Chrome 152
openQuestions.detail: On a 152+ browser, confirm the clip strip's scrollTop stays 0 after scrollIntoView while scrollLeft still centres card 8, and capture the emerald 'pinned at 0' readout. A follow-up concept could combine scroll clip with scroll-snap-type x mandatory to explore the SingleAxisScrollContainersForScrollSnap dependency flag.

guidanceConsulted.query: horizontal scroll carousel keyboard accessible scroll region
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: When bringing an element into view in a scrollable list, use scrollIntoView with explicit inline/block alignment rather than manual offset maths.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The demo's primary action uses scrollIntoView({inline:'center', block:'nearest'}) — the exact API whose block-axis side effect on hidden vs clip axes the feature changes — and the copy explains the alignment choice.

guidanceConsulted.query: overflow clip vs hidden scrolling behavior
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: overflow: clip prevents both user and programmatic scrolling; hidden blocks only user scrolling.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The two strips are a side-by-side embodiment of this rule, and the what-to-look-for section states it explicitly so the visual difference is explained in guidance-accurate terms.

summary: The practical payoff demo: identical carousels under scroll hidden vs scroll clip, with scrollIntoView and raw script scrolling as the attack vectors and per-strip live readouts as the evidence. On coerced browsers both strips misbehave identically and the page says so in the banner and readouts rather than faking the new behavior.
